title: Render driveable roads and physics collision
acceptance: compiled road and intersection meshes render in Three.js at the expected one-to-one scale and connect cleanly across active tile boundaries
Rapier receives road collision geometry only for the configured physics-active tile region and removes it when those tiles deactivate
road geometry follows compiled roadbed/intersection surfaces rather than drawing fixed-width ribbons from centerlines
direction/lane/road-class metadata remains accessible for debugging and future presentation even though traffic rules are not enforced in the initial free-drive mode

static collision tests prove tile activation is idempotent, roadbed contact is queryable, and collision planes are removed/rebased cleanly; dynamic player traversal across tile seams is explicitly verified by T007 because T006 precedes the vehicle implementation
verification: PR #5 merged into main as 27354af039933299f411c164c41f78de2df1bc05 after clean hosted verification. npm run check passed with TypeScript, 11 Vitest tests including real Rapier WASM ray contact, and a Vite production build. Roach project health, lint/schema, Ubuntu coordination, and Windows coordination also passed. Three.js triangulation-index handling, strict noUncheckedIndexedAccess bounds checks, upward road triangle winding, and Rapier world-query refresh behavior were corrected before merge.

evidence.work: Roadbed-derived Three.js meshes and streamed Rapier trimesh collision, one collider per physics-active tile, metadata-preserving centerline debug objects, collider rebasing/removal, and real Rapier contact tests merged via PR #5. Dynamic seam traversal is transferred to T007 where a dynamic player vehicle exists.
